steps.intro: Meet the sounds and shapes of Greek before any rules. Read each line aloud, then check the English.

cards.title: Alpha with Angela, lesson 1
cards.note: Optional: a short lesson taught entirely in Greek, with pictures. It uses the same pronunciation as this app. Come back here when it ends.

cards.en: In the beginning was the Word,

cards.text: καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν,
cards.say: kai ho LO-gos ayn pros ton the-ON
cards.en: and the Word was with God,

cards.title: Greek reads like English
body: Greek runs left to right, and many letters look familiar: ο is o, κ is k, ς is s at the end of a word.
Some look like English letters but sound different: ν is n, not v, and ρ is r, not p. Others are new, such as λ (l) and θ (th as in thin). You will learn all 24 in the alphabet lesson.

cards.title: Endings show a word's job
body: Look at God in this verse: θεόν after πρός (with), but θεός in “the Word was God”. Greek changes a word's ending to show what it is doing in the sentence.
“The” changes too: ὁ λόγος (the Word) but τὸν θεόν (with God). You will meet these patterns properly in the lessons on nouns and cases; for now, just notice them.

cards.explain: λόγος is “word”. In John 1:1 it is a title for Jesus, the Word.
θεός (the-OS) is God, the root of English words like theology.

cards.prompt: Match each Greek word to its meaning.
Put the words in order: “In the beginning was the Word”.
cards.explain: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος. Here the Greek order matches the English word for word.
ἦν is “he, she or it was”: one person or thing, in the past. Grammar books call this the third person singular imperfect of εἰμί, “I am”.

steps.intro: Now read the real verses. Words you have met are underlined in gold; tap any word to see what it means.

cards.note: οὗτος means “he” or “this one”. You already know every other word.
